citation: AND-cross-composition: disjoint union of 3-SAT instances — primal treewidth of the union = max over parts, and ∧φ_i is satisfiable iff every φ_i is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: SAT by primal treewidth is FPT (2^tw·poly DP). Disjoint union is a clean AND-cross-composition (parameter = max tw ≤ single-instance size), so no polynomial kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard 3-SAT via disjoint union (tw = max; conjunction satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: 3-SAT by treewidth is FPT; same disjoint-union AND-composition as the sat row rules out a poly kernel.

citation: 2k-vertex kernel via Nemhauser–Trotter LP (Math. Programming 1975) / crown decomposition; Chen–Kanj–Xia. Textbook: Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms (2015), ch. 2.
note: Classic 2k-vertex polynomial kernel for Vertex Cover parameterized by solution size k.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard 3-Coloring via disjoint union: tw(union)=max, and the union is 3-colorable iff every component is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly. Cf. BJK's stated result 'Clique parameterized by treewidth admits no poly kernel'.
note: 3-Coloring by treewidth is FPT (3^tw·poly). Disjoint-union AND-composition gives no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly.

citation: Blažej, Choudhary, Knop, Schierreich, Suchý, Valla, 'On Polynomial Kernels for TSP and its Generalizations', IPEC 2022 (arXiv:2207.01109), Lemma 1 + Lemma 57: Hamiltonian Path AND-cross-composes into TSP parameterized by (treewidth + maximum degree); no poly kernel unless PH collapses.
note: TSP/Hamiltonicity is FPT by treewidth (2^O(tw) rank-based/Cut&Count). Lower bound is stated for the larger combined parameter tw+Δ, so a fortiori no poly kernel for treewidth alone (tw ≤ tw+Δ).

citation: Mahajan–Raman, 'Parameterizing above guaranteed values: MaxSat and MaxCut', J. Algorithms 31(2):335–354 (1999): cut ≥ m/2 + k is FPT with a poly (O(k)-edge) kernel. Strengthened above the tighter Edwards–Erdős bound: Crowston–Jones–Mnich (ICALP 2012, Algorithmica) O(k^5); Etscheid–Mnich O(k).
note: Above-m/2 parameterization has a polynomial (indeed linear) kernel.

citation: Thomassé, 'A 4k^2 kernel for feedback vertex set', ACM Trans. Algorithms 6(2):32 (2010).

Dom, Lokshtanov, Saurabh, 'Incompressibility through Colors and IDs', ICALP 2009: Steiner Tree parameterized by (#terminals + solution size) has no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly (colors-and-IDs composition).
note: FPT by #terminals (Dreyfus–Wagner 3^ℓ / Björklund et al. 2^ℓ). Lower bound for the larger param (terminals+k) propagates to #terminals alone; no poly kernel.

citation: Bodlaender, Downey, Fellows, Hermelin, 'On problems without polynomial kernels', JCSS 75(8):423–434 (2009): k-Path has no poly kernel unless coNP⊆NP/poly via OR-composition (disjoint union of graphs; a k-vertex path lives in one component).
note: Canonical OR-composition example. FPT by color-coding; no polynomial kernel.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard NAE-3-SAT (Schaefer) via disjoint union (tw = max; NAE-satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: NAE-SAT by treewidth is FPT; disjoint-union AND-composition rules out a poly kernel, same convention as sat-3.

parameterization: number of distinct item sizes d
citation: Goemans–Rothvoß (SODA 2014) and Jansen–Klein solve Bin Packing with d distinct sizes in time (log Δ)^(2^(2^d)) — XP (poly for fixed d), explicitly NOT an f(d)·poly FPT algorithm.
note: FPT in the number of distinct item sizes is itself a KNOWN OPEN problem (only XP is known); with FPT unresolved no poly kernel can be claimed. The atlas 'FPT in #distinct item sizes' overstates the literature — hence kernel status open.

parameterization: number of distinct job (processing) types, identical machines
citation: FPT via integer programming in fixed dimension (Lenstra 1983 / Kannan; configuration ILP) — e.g. Cygan et al. (2015) ILP applications. No poly kernel known and no lower bound located for this parameter.
note: Parameter-sensitive: #machines alone is para-NP-hard (NP-hard at m=2, Partition); #job types on related/unrelated machines is para-NP-hard (NP-hard at 6 types); polynomial kernels are known only for the DIFFERENT parameter p_max (Knop et al., 'Scheduling Kernels via Configuration LP', arXiv:2003.02187, ESA 2022). Under the only FPT reading (identical machines, #distinct job types) no poly kernel is known.

citation: Blažej, Choudhary, Knop, Schierreich, Suchý, Valla, IPEC 2022 (arXiv:2207.01109), Lemma 1: Hamiltonian Path AND-cross-composes into TSP parameterized by (treewidth + max degree); no poly kernel unless PH collapses.
note: Same canonical parameter and treatment as the tsp row; lower bound for tw+Δ gives no poly kernel for treewidth alone. (Note: literal metric completion has treewidth n−1; the atlas means the TSP-family problem by input-graph treewidth.)

citation: AND-cross-composition from Holyer's NP-hard 3-edge-coloring of cubic graphs (SICOMP 10(4):718–720, 1981): disjoint union of cubic graphs is cubic (Δ=3), tw = max, and is 3-edge-colorable iff every component is. Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: Edge-coloring (chromatic index) is FPT by treewidth (Zhou–Nakano–Nishizeki, edge-coloring partial k-trees). Disjoint-union AND-composition on cubic instances rules out a poly kernel.

citation: FPT: Marx, 'Parameterized graph separation problems', Theoret. Comput. Sci. 351(3):394–406 (2006), important separators; O*(2^k) in Cygan et al. Best kernel is 2^O(k); a quasipolynomial kernel k^{(log k)^O(1)} is known (Wahlström, 'Quasipolynomial multicut-mimicking networks and kernelization', ICALP 2020 / arXiv:2002.08825).
note: General (unbounded-terminal) Multiway Cut by solution size: no polynomial kernel is known, and no coNP⊆NP/poly lower bound exists — indeed the quasipolynomial kernel makes one unlikely. Honest FPT-no-poly-known (poly kernels known only for bounded #terminals, O(k^{s+1}), or planar graphs).

citation: Abu-Khzam, 'A quadratic kernel for 3-Set Packing', TAMC 2009 (O(k^2) elements); d-Set Matching has O(k^d)-edge kernels with a matching O(k^{d-ε}) lower bound: Dell–Marx, 'Kernelization of packing problems', SODA 2012.
note: Polynomial (essentially tight) kernel for k-3DM / 3-Set Packing by solution size.

citation: AND-cross-composition from NP-hard Positive-1-in-3-SAT (Schaefer) via disjoint union (tw = max; 1-in-3-satisfiable iff all parts are). Bodlaender–Jansen–Kratsch cross-composition (STACS 2011; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 28(1):277–305, 2014); Drucker (FOCS 2012) established that AND-cross-composition also rules out poly kernels unless coNP⊆NP/poly.
note: 1-in-3-SAT by treewidth is FPT; disjoint-union AND-composition rules out a poly kernel (SAT-family convention, same as sat-3/nae-sat).

citation: FPT by treewidth via 2^tw CSP dynamic programming. No poly kernel known; no kernelization lower bound located for MAX-2LIN (or its special case MAX-CUT) parameterized by the treewidth of the instance.
note: As a MAX/threshold problem, disjoint union yields neither a clean AND- nor OR-composition (unlike the satisfy-all CSPs sat-3/nae-sat/1-in-3), so the standard treewidth lower-bound route does not directly apply and no citation was found. The general treewidth heuristic suggests a lower bound likely exists, but it is not citable here — honest FPT-no-poly-known. Distinct from the well-settled above-guarantee Max-Cut (which has a poly kernel).

citation: Chen–Meng, 'A 2k kernel for the cluster editing problem', JCSS 78(1):211–220 (2012); earlier 4k kernel via critical cliques: Guo, 'A more effective linear kernelization for cluster editing', Theoret. Comput. Sci. 410(8–10):718–726 (2009).
note: Linear 2k-vertex polynomial kernel for cluster editing by edit budget k.
